name: Hazari
description: Hazari (meaning 'One Thousand') is a highly strategic partitioning game popular in Bangladesh and Bhutan. Players receive 13 cards and must divide them into four sets (composed of 3, 3, 3, and 4 cards). These sets are then compared against opponents' sets in a fixed order. The game combines the hand-ranking logic of Brag and Teen Patti with a unique structural challenge and a long-term scoring goal of 1000 points.

content.text: Hazari (meaning 'One Thousand') is a highly strategic partitioning game popular in Bangladesh and Bhutan. Players receive 13 cards and must divide them into four sets (composed of 3, 3, 3, and 4 cards). These sets are then compared against opponents' sets in a fixed order. The game combines the hand-ranking logic of Brag and Teen Patti with a unique structural challenge and a long-term scoring goal of 1000 points.

Originating in South Asia, Hazari is closely related to the British game 'Crash' (or Thirteen-card Brag). It has become the most popular card game in Bangladesh, often played in tea stalls and social clubs.
Dealer deals 13 cards to each player in batches (e.g., 4-4-5 or all at once).

items.text: Hazarey (Bhutan): A variant popular in Bhutan with slightly different scoring for numeral cards.
